about: Dating length before marriage. HCMST 2009 married couples (held-out test, ../reproducibility/dating_length/) and verified published estimates. Built by reproducibility/dating_length/scripts/export_app.py; aggregates only.

grade.label: retrospective surveys; held-out test null
grade.reason: Not applied to any lens number: HCMST shows no held-out gain, and the only verified hazard ratios come from an opt-in online retrospective survey that the evidence review marks not usable in the app.

audit.note: Odds ratios are per follow-up period, from one unpenalised fit (no interval); the held-out comparison is the test.

literature.contrast: Dated 3+ years before proposal vs <1 year (all persons)
literature.population: US online survey (SurveyMonkey Audience) of ever-married adults, weighted to ACS
literature.adjusted_for: age, marriage age, sex, race, education, employment, household income, region, religious attendance, spouse age/race/education differences, children, knew spouse well, dating length, attitudes, honeymoon, ring cost, attendance, wedding cost
literature.citation: Francis-Tan, A., & Mialon, H. M. (2015). "A diamond is forever" and other fairy tales: The relationship between wedding expenses and marriage duration. Economic Inquiry, 53(4), 1919-1930.
literature.locator: Table 2 (population-weighted Cox regressions; columns: Bivariate All Persons; Multivariate All Persons; Men Only; Women Only). "Hazard ratios are reported with standard errors in parentheses." Stars: * 10%, ** 5%, *** 1%. Value = Multivariate All
literature.caveats: Opt-in online sample, retrospective recall of costs; many covariates (some arguably mediators); significance at 10% flagged as *.
